# Product Vocabulary

<!-- @generated by `node scripts/conformance/run.mjs --write` from contracts/vocabulary/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Registry revision 2 (`vocabulary@2`, which is `DR-0001@2`), additive. The decision record is [`DR-0001`](decisions/DR-0001-product-vocabulary.json); owner items are in [`DR-0001-owner-corrections.md`](decisions/DR-0001-owner-corrections.md).

Every name a user sees and every domain term an implementer uses comes from [`contracts/vocabulary/terms.json`](../contracts/vocabulary/terms.json). A baseline name that differs has an entry in [`adapters.json`](../contracts/vocabulary/adapters.json) naming the leaf that retires it. [`leaf-ids.json`](../contracts/vocabulary/leaf-ids.json) lists every leaf ID a file may cite.

## Using It

- UI code takes user-visible names from `frontend/src/vocabulary/labels.ts`. `label('extracted-claim')` returns "Proposed change", and `label('pursuit', { option: 'pipeline-item', count: 2 })` returns "Pipeline items". Internal and inspection-only terms have no label; history, provenance, and inspection surfaces use `inspectionTerms`.
- A leaf that depends on these names cites `DR-0001@2` in its `consumes`.
- Existing copy keeps its adapter entry until its retiring leaf replaces it. Remove the entry in that PR.
- To change a term, edit `terms.json`, raise `revision` there and in `DR-0001`, mark `compatibility` additive or breaking, regenerate, and get the record re-approved (its `approvalRef` pins the file's SHA-256). A breaking revision keeps a `term` adapter entry for each removed name.
- A new name in the coverage set needs a term label or an adapter entry. Never loosen the rule.
- Check with `node scripts/conformance/run.mjs` and `node --test scripts/conformance` (Node 22, no install). `--write` regenerates this file, `labels.ts`, and the owner corrections file. CI runs both in the `conformance` job.

## Positioning

> Rounds is a self-hostable career command center that connects a person's canonical professional history and evidence to the opportunities they pursue, the artifacts they submit, the interviews they prepare for, the practice they complete, and the next actions they should take.

Title form: Career Command Center. Source: rounds-review PRODUCT.md:45-48 (decision P1).

## Terms

Visibility: `user-facing` terms have a label; `inspection-only` terms appear only on history, provenance, and inspection surfaces (spec 1016-1017); `internal` terms never appear in the UI. A term marked ratified-here, or a label marked [G6] to [G9], comes from a decision beyond spec text and is pending owner approval. The default option is bold when a term has several.

- **Account** (`account`): Owns authentication identity, security controls, provider connections, product preferences, appearance preferences, locale and accessibility preferences, and data-retention preferences. It does not own professional history or target-opportunity facts; the current Profile page becomes Account.
- **Account preference** (`account-preference`): A product, appearance, locale and accessibility, or data-retention preference owned by Account, including the current campaign selection, which only sets query defaults.
- **Account and Settings** (`account-and-settings`): Primary navigation destination for Account identity, security controls, provider connections, and Account preferences, kept separate from professional profile editing.
- **Sign-in provider** (`sign-in-provider`): An external identity provider an Account signs in with, such as an OAuth provider. "Provider" is always qualified.
- **AI provider** (`ai-provider`): An AI model provider connection the Account configures. Its credential lives in the account secret store and is used only through the provider gateway. "Provider" is always qualified.
- **Calendar provider** (`calendar-provider`): An external calendar service reached through the calendar connector contract. Continuous synchronization is a separate integration workstream. "Provider" is always qualified.
- **Privacy class** (`privacy-class`): One of the five normative classes (Private, Sensitive, Third-party personal, Secret, Share Projection) that set what may reach remote AI, search, logs and traces, public share, and export, local draft, and backup. A career pack may make a rule stricter but cannot relax it. Defined by #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01).
- **Private** (`privacy-private`): Private, the default: profile facts, opportunities, actions, and ordinary practice. Remote AI needs per-request consent after a payload preview; search and index stay inside the owning account; logs and traces carry metadata and opaque IDs only; public share only through a separately reviewed Share Projection; account export, account-namespaced local drafts, and encrypted backup are allowed. Defined by #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01).
- **Sensitive** (`privacy-sensitive`): Compensation, immigration, accommodation, private feedback, and protected demographics. Remote AI is off by default with a separate field-level confirmation for one invocation; search is off by default or masked with explicit opt-in; logs and traces carry no field values or reversible identifiers; excluded from public share by default, and sharing needs a separate confirmation and a scoped snapshot; protected export only, with encrypted local draft and backup. Defined by #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01).
- **Third-party personal** (`privacy-third-party-personal`): Recruiter, interviewer, and contact identity, messages, and notes about another person. Remote AI is off by default with purpose-specific confirmation; search stays account-local; logs and traces carry minimized pseudonymous IDs; excluded from public share unless that exact field is intentionally published; included in full account export with a warning, with encrypted local draft and backup. Defined by #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01).
- **Secret** (`privacy-secret`): Provider credentials, reset and session tokens, share bearer material, and encryption keys. Never sent to remote AI, indexed, logged, or shared. Excluded from normal export and browser storage; only an explicit rewrapped secret export; encrypted backup with separate key custody. Defined by #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01).
- **Share Projection** (`privacy-share-projection`): Owner-reviewed fields from one immutable Artifact Revision. Never part of remote AI resolution; not added to public indexing; an aggregate view event only when enabled; shared only through its scoped capability; exportable immutable bytes with no browser draft and an encrypted backup of the owner record. Defined by #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01).

- **Career Profile** (`career-profile`): The aggregate root for canonical professional facts. It references typed records rather than storing one undifferentiated document. Profile records support stable identity, revision history, source provenance, confidence when derived, relationships, visibility and privacy classification, and career-pack extensions.
- **Professional Identity** (`professional-identity`): Career Profile construct for how the person is identified professionally: professional name and headline (one per Career Profile).
- **Contact Point** (`contact-point`): Career Profile construct for one typed way to reach the person, such as email, phone, or location; one Career Profile has many.
- **External Profile** (`external-profile`): Career Profile construct for an external profile or link, such as a portfolio or public code profile. Spec label: "External Profile or Link".
- **Engagement** (`engagement`): Career Profile construct for employment or another engagement the person held; employment and project facts are many Career Profile records. Spec label: "Engagement or Role".
- **Project** (`project`): Career Profile construct for a project or work sample. Spec label: "Project or Work Sample".
- **Achievement** (`achievement`): Career Profile construct for an achievement or the evidence behind it. Spec label: "Achievement or Evidence".
- **Narrative** (`narrative`): Career Profile construct for a professional narrative or story, including behavioral stories. Spec label: "Narrative or Story".
- **Skill** (`skill`): Career Profile construct for a skill or competency; packs add profession-specific facets. Spec label: "Skill or Competency".
- **Education** (`education`): Career Profile construct for education or a credential. Spec label: "Education or Credential".
- **Publication** (`publication`): Career Profile construct for a publication.
- **Preference** (`preference`): Career Profile construct for a job-search preference or constraint, such as target role, location, or work policy. Account preferences are a different term (Setting). Spec label: "Preference or Constraint".

### Evidence

| Term | ID | Label | Visibility | Owning leaf | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider Invocation Intent | `provider-invocation-intent` |  | inspection-only | #73 (ROUNDS-14-L02) | spec 693-714, 726 |
| Provider Invocation Outcome | `provider-invocation-outcome` |  | inspection-only | #73 (ROUNDS-14-L02) | spec 700-701, 716-724 |
| Provider Invocation Receipt | `provider-invocation-receipt` |  | inspection-only | #73 (ROUNDS-14-L02) | spec 693-701, 745-747, 761-762 |

- **Provider Invocation Intent** (`provider-invocation-intent`): An immutable record committed before any provider egress: purpose and capability; account, command, source, Processing Attempt, and retry-lineage identifiers; consent, privacy-, retention-, and redaction-policy versions; the exact source-version vector; outbound payload digest; provider endpoint identity, model revision, parameters, prompt-contract version, tool policy, and provider idempotency key; authorization; and intended retention. No network request occurs until the Intent commit succeeds.
- **Provider Invocation Outcome** (`provider-invocation-outcome`): An immutable record linked to one Intent, committed after response, failure, cancellation, or reconciliation and before any result is applied: provider request and response identifiers and digests, dispatch, response, and persistence timestamps, succeeded, failed, canceled, or unknown-after-egress state, failure class and token accounting, a Staged Provider Result ID for every success, and final retention.
- **Provider Invocation Receipt** (`provider-invocation-receipt`): Logical envelope of an immutable pre-egress Intent and immutable post-egress Outcome for one model attempt. It proves what policy and inputs governed one invocation without retaining sensitive plaintext.

- **Source Document** (`source-document`): Preserves material submitted for parsing or reference: file or pasted text, source URL and retrieval metadata, media type, checksum, retention and privacy policy, extraction status, parser and model version, and previous processing attempts.
- **Processing Attempt** (`processing-attempt`): One durable parsing, OCR, URL retrieval, repository analysis, extraction, or reprocessing attempt, in queued, leased, succeeded, failed, canceled, superseded, or stale state, with source checksum, idempotency key, lease, bounded retry, and cancellation.
- **Staged Provider Result** (`staged-provider-result`): The privacy-classed, encrypted, retention-bounded normalized result of one successful provider response, linked to one Outcome: versioned extraction or generation payload, source anchors, validation result, response digest, and the deterministic seed that recreates identical claims or proposals without another provider call.
- **Capture Center** (`capture-center`): The one capture surface, opened from every page and the Command Center, through which manual entry, natural-language quick capture, paste, files, job-posting URLs, JSON Resume, LinkedIn export, GitHub, and later pack sources feed the common command and ingestion model. Source material is preserved even when extraction fails. Aliases: "Global Capture".

- **Entity Version** (`entity-version`): Concurrency token for one mutable record. Aliases: "Provider/session version", "Profile/Entity Version".
- **Aggregate Revision** (`aggregate-revision`): Ordered domain state for one aggregate. Aliases: "Expected-version command history", "Append-only accepted revision".
- **Transaction Change Set** (`transaction-change-set`): One atomic command result that may touch multiple aggregates, identified by account and command ID. Rolling back creates a compensating change set against current expected versions; it never rewinds history blindly.
- **Profile Revision** (`profile-revision`): Named Career Profile change set.
- **Offer Revision** (`offer-revision`): Immutable complete offer terms. Each accepted change to an Offer creates one, containing the complete terms, source, actor, timestamp, deadline, and prior revision.
- **Audit Entry** (`audit-entry`): Immutable record of an authorized mutation: what changed, who or what requested it, authorization context, previous and current versions, and the transaction change set. It is not the user-facing Interview Round or Offer model.
- **Domain Event** (`domain-event`): Immutable outbox and integration message emitted after the same transaction commits, with schema version, aggregate sequence, causation ID, correlation ID, account scope, and change-set position.
- **Opportunity Revision** (`opportunity-revision`): Revision of an Opportunity's role posting and job description. One Opportunity may have many source revisions; a referenced revision is retained when the Opportunity is archived.
- **Relation Version** (`relation-version`): Version of one typed relation, such as Pursuit-to-Campaign membership, which changes only by explicit detach.
- **Edition Version** (`edition-version`): Version of an Artifact Edition's wording overrides; removing an override affects future revisions only.
- **Preference Version** (`preference-version`): Version of one Account preference, such as the current campaign selection.
- **Key Version** (`key-version`): Version of a key in the account secret store; revoking it crypto-deletes what it protected.
- **Capability Version** (`capability-version`): Version of one Share Capability; revocation and expiry take effect immediately.
- **Activation Version** (`activation-version`): Activation and version state of one Pack Activation.
- **Projection Watermark** (`projection-watermark`): Freshness position of a derived read model, Readiness Snapshot, or search index against its sources.
- **Algorithm Version** (`algorithm-version`): Version of the algorithm or projector that derived a read model, Readiness Snapshot, Recommendation, or search index. Aliases: "Projector version".

In UI copy, "workspace" means only this. Aliases: "Workspace".

- **Pursuit** (`pursuit`): The user's active or historical relationship with an opportunity. Owns pipeline stage, stage history, dates, disposition, user notes, campaign membership, priority and fit assessment, and relations to people, materials, actions, interview process, and offers. "Application" remains valid user-facing language once a pursuit has been submitted; wishlist and networking stages exist before an application does. Spec label: "Application, Opportunity, or Pipeline item according to stage".
- **Interview Process** (`interview-process`): Owns only the structured hiring-process definition for one Pursuit: optional loops or stages, ordered references to interview Career Activities, default round types and expected signals, default preparation context, and derived progress and outcome summaries. It owns no writable schedule, participant, debrief, outcome, or reschedule history.
- **Offer** (`offer`): The current comparable negotiation aggregate; zero or more per Pursuit. Each accepted change creates an immutable Offer Revision. Offer state and Pursuit state connect through explicit transition rules; one component never silently rewrites another's status.
- **Campaign/Goal** (`campaign-goal`): A user-defined planning goal and time box: name and intent, date range, lifecycle, target criteria, explicit Pursuit membership, optional preparation objective, display preferences, and progress projections. It is a lens over canonical records; interview rounds, Actions, and attempts derive campaign context through their owning Pursuit or an explicit goal relation. Aliases: "Campaign or Goal", "Goal".
- **Pipeline** (`pipeline`): Primary navigation destination for Pursuits: stage-based and list views from one pursuit model, opportunity source health, fit and priority, campaign lenses, saved filters, clear wishlist, networking, and application semantics, and degraded-data indicators. Applications and separate round management become Pipeline and the Opportunity Workspace.

- **Action** (`action`): Owns work to be done: title and body, status, due date and optional schedule, priority, effort estimate, recurrence when supported, relations to canonical entities, origin or recommendation reason, and completion effect. Rich-text mentions may render relations, but text does not own relationship identity. Todos become Actions. Aliases: "Task".
- **Recommendation** (`recommendation`): A stable recommendation identity derived from an input vector and algorithm version. It can expire or be dismissed, snoozed, or invalidated, and feeds Today and Action creation; it becomes an Action only when accepted.
- **Today** (`today`): Primary navigation destination that explains the few actions that matter, why they matter, and what changes when they are completed: a short prioritized narrative queue, not a card index of every subsystem.
- **Command Center** (`command-center`): Keyboard entry point for universal search, create and capture, navigation, domain commands, recent entities, campaign lens switching, and pending import review. Quick and full forms use the same field definitions and commands.

Owns artifact type, purpose, target opportunity or audience, selected profile facts, order and grouping, explicit wording overrides, design and template configuration, source profile revision, generated output revisions, submission and freeze state, and export and share history. An edition does not become a second editable career database. Resume Studio and cover-letter generation become Materials. Spec label: "Resume, Cover Letter, Interview Brief, or Material".
- **Artifact Revision** (`artifact-revision`): Immutable materialized content and renderer contract: content snapshot, source entity-version map, accepted override values, opportunity revision, template, renderer, font, and asset versions, locale and pagination inputs, byte checksums for retained exports, and creation, submission, and share metadata. A submitted material and a public share always reference one exact Artifact Revision. Spec label: "Version or Submitted version".
- **Generation Proposal** (`generation-proposal`): AI-authored wording or synthesis, which is not an Extracted Claim. It records task and target artifact, source entity-version map, supporting passages or facts, generated text, model and provider and prompt-contract version, unsupported-claim warnings, reviewer edits, accept or reject decision, and the resulting Artifact Revision when accepted.
- **Legacy Artifact Snapshot** (`legacy-artifact-snapshot`): A strictly transitional containment bridge: immutable and account-scoped, created only by an authenticated server command after verifying ownership of the current resume, variant, or version, materialized from server-read legacy records and never caller-authored HTML. It stores legacy source IDs and versions, sanitized content, bounded render options, template, font, asset, and renderer versions, and an output checksum or retained bytes; it cannot be edited or treated as canonical career data and is rendered or shared only through the contained worker and capability contracts. ROUNDS-15 migrates each one to an Artifact Revision and retires it once nothing references it.
- **Artifact Renderer Contract** (`artifact-renderer-contract`): The trusted, versioned, server-owned contract through which the server materializes markup to render an Artifact Edition, Artifact Revision, or Legacy Artifact Snapshot. The public API never accepts caller-authored HTML, JavaScript, browser flags, filesystem paths, network policy, or renderer commands.
- **Share Capability** (`share-capability`): A narrow, unguessable read capability scoped to one immutable Artifact Revision or containment-era Legacy Artifact Snapshot. Only a keyed digest of the bearer token is stored, cleartext bearer material is disclosed once, and expiry, password policy, revocation, and view policy are recorded. It never grants administrative record access, and revocation invalidates it immediately. Aliases: "Public share".

- **Practice Item** (`practice-item`): Pack-owned practice content keyed (pack, track, slug). A Practice Attempt pins one Practice Item and its career-pack version. AI-coding rounds are Practice Items. Aliases: "Question", "Problem", "Assignment". Defined by #39 (ROUNDS-07-L01).
- **Practice Draft** (`practice-draft`): Mutable work in progress on a Practice Item, kept separate from immutable attempts.
- **Practice Session** (`practice-session`): An active practice session, such as a running timer, kept as a mutable record separate from immutable attempts.
- **Practice Attempt** (`practice-attempt`): An immutable result tied to a Practice Item and career-pack version, candidate inputs and durable work artifacts, server-owned harness and test version, execution-environment version, result and evidence, feedback, duration and timestamps, opportunity and campaign context, and causation and correlation identifiers.
- **Execution Attempt** (`execution-attempt`): One server-side run or evaluation of candidate code under the execution-control protocol and its durable result envelope. It is not a Practice Attempt. Defined by #3 (ROUNDS-00A-L03).
- **Test Definition** (`test-definition`): A server-owned, immutable, versioned definition of the tests an execution request is evaluated against. Clients send candidate source and structured input only, never shell commands, executable validators, hidden tests, or expected-result code.
- **Harness Revision** (`harness-revision`): A server-owned, immutable, versioned harness. Any expressive validator runs inside the same isolated worker as candidate code, never through eval in the API or control plane.
- **Readiness Snapshot** (`readiness-snapshot`): A versioned, pack-owned readiness projection with a projection watermark and algorithm version, rebuilt or purged deterministically and read by Today and the preparation plan.
- **Practice** (`practice`): Primary navigation destination for the career-pack practice tracks, Practice Items and Attempts, opportunity context, preparation plans, readiness, history, and feedback. Existing strong practice pages stay recognizable behind the pack contract.

- **Career Pack** (`career-pack`): A trusted, reviewed bundle shipped at build time that extends the stable platform core through a versioned manifest: extension schemas, field definitions, validators, relation types, editors and renderers, import aliases, interview-process and round types, practice tracks, attempt schemas, artifact projectors, readiness signals, recommendation contributors, search contributions, migrations, and required capabilities. Packs cannot redefine platform terms.
- **Pack Activation** (`pack-activation`): Account or deployment activation of a pack manifest already shipped with the deployment, atomic across platform contract, schema and handlers, editors and renderers, migrations, projectors, and search contributions. State is inactive, migrating, active, read-only, incompatible, or failed; deactivation keeps pack data read-only.
- **System Design** (`track-system-design`): Software Engineering practice track for system design guides, questions, diagrams, practice canvas, status, drafts, and timers. Aliases: "system".
- **Coding** (`track-coding`): Software Engineering practice track for coding lists, the editor, drafts, focus mode, custom runs, evaluation, status, and timers.
- **AI-Assisted Coding** (`track-ai-coding`): Software Engineering practice track for AI-assisted coding files, checkpoints, chat and edit, runner, grade, drafts, and attempts. Aliases: "AI Assisted Coding", "ai-assisted-coding".
- **Take-Home** (`track-take-home`): Software Engineering practice track for real-world and take-home prompts, files, harness, AI policy, rubric, drafts, and attempts. Aliases: "Real World Problems", "Real-World Problem", "real-world", "builder".
- **Behavioral** (`track-behavioral`): Software Engineering practice track for behavioral guides, questions, categories, story links, status, and timers.

## Shared Labels

- "Role": `opportunity` and `engagement` (spec 1003, spec 418; G5, SCR-ROLE).
- "Opportunity": `opportunity` and `pursuit` (spec 1003, spec 1004; G5).

## Usage Rules

- G3: "Attempt" labels only Practice Attempt. Execution Attempt and Processing Attempt are inspection-only.
- G4: "Profile" alone is never a label. The Profile page is Account; Career Profile is the only profile.
- G6: In UI copy, "workspace" means only the Opportunity Workspace.
- G7: Account preferences are labeled "Setting"; "Preference" stays with the profile construct.
- G7: "Provider" is always qualified: Sign-in provider, AI provider, Calendar provider.
- G7: In UI copy, "Capability" means only Share Capability.
- G7: In "X or Y", the first name is canonical and the second is a label option.

## Namespaces

- `platform`: Stable platform terms. Career packs cannot redefine them (spec 815-840).
- `pack.software-engineering` (provisional): Provisional namespace for the Software Engineering pack until #39 takes it over under pack ID software-engineering.

Platform core (spec 815-840): Account, Career Profile identity, Organization, Person, Opportunity, Pursuit, Career Activity, Interview Process, Offer, Campaign/Goal, Practice Attempt envelope, Audit Entry and Domain Event envelopes, Action, Artifact Edition envelope, Source Document, Claim, Staged Provider Result, Provider Invocation Receipt, Revision, authorization, provenance, transaction semantics. No pack term, alias, or label may equal one of these or a platform term.

## Dispositions

Features (spec 335-337, 341-374, G10). Optional text after the value, such as "and harden" or "without loss".

- `Preserve`: Behavior remains recognizably intact.
- `Transform`: The capability remains but its model or interaction changes.
- `Retire`: Requires explicit owner approval and a replacement or migration statement.

Data items (spec 2649-2673):

- `migrate`: Migrate with a field-level algorithm.
- `archive`: Preserve as an immutable opaque archive.
- `rebuild`: Rebuild deterministically.
- `reconcile`: Re-enter through a client-assisted reconciliation flow.
- `drop`: Intentionally drop, only after explicit owner approval.

Catalog words: bridge is `migrate` with a time-bounded adapter the transferring leaf owns; quarantine is `archive`; retire is `drop` only with owner approval.

## Data-Preserving Clean Cutover

The transformation moves one bounded context at a time. Temporary expand/contract schemas, compatibility adapters, shadow reads, and migration comparison are allowed. Each converted concept has one writable authority, an explicit retirement criterion, and a time-bounded compatibility window. This avoids both permanent dual-writing and one high-risk whole-product cutover. (spec 2637-2647, G11)

Write it as "data-preserving clean cutover". The check rejects the phrase without "data-preserving" anywhere in the repository except these shipped migration lines, which are never edited: `pocketbase/pb_migrations/1700004100_drop_legacy_anecdotes.js:3`, `pocketbase/pb_migrations/1700005100_drop_resume_bullets.js:3`, `docs/program/non-goals.json:179`.

## Adapters

164 entries: 50 collection, 3 field, 19 stored-value, 8 api-route, 31 route-segment, 28 ui-string, 20 app-header, 3 positioning, 2 doc. Each maps a baseline name to a term or to the leaf that decides it, gives the label it becomes, and names the retiring leaf: the leaf that renames or removes the name, or confirms it as a canonical internal name.

## Coverage Set

The check extracts these names from the repository and maps each to a term label or an adapter entry:

- `collection`: PocketBase collections created or dropped by `up` migrations in `pocketbase/pb_migrations/`, plus the built-in `users`. Dropped ones are historical. A non-literal name needs adapter entries whose `source.lines` cover the call. #155 (ROUNDS-32-L01) takes this over once its store registry lands.
- `stored-value`: `user_progress.question_type` and `user_progress.status` select values, and the `INTERVIEW_TYPES` keys (and aliases) stored in `interview_rounds.round_type`.
- `api-route`: the prefix of each router `backend/main.py` mounts, and its direct routes such as `/health`.
- `route-segment`: literal path segments of `<Route path>` and `<Navigate to>` in `frontend/src/App.tsx`.
- `ui-string`: navigation labels, user-menu destinations, and sidebar headings in `Layout.tsx`, and each Command Center entry's label and description in `command-center/registry.tsx`.
- `app-header`: literal `eyebrow` and `title` props at every `<AppHeader>` call site under `frontend/src`.
- `positioning`: `README.md` lines 1 and 3, `docs/architecture.md` line 3, `frontend/index.html` line 17, `Login.tsx` line 239, and `SHOWCASE.md` line 3.

UI strings and AppHeader props that equal a term's label are covered by the term; everything else needs an adapter entry.

## Leaf IDs

176 filed leaves (#1 to #176 in catalog order), pinned to rounds-review src/data/capabilities.json sha256 `1ca5cfbb496e25a9c5d0e9b3e949c569d1d1bd628b67a971e8fce53dc9b02988`. 6 proposed: #177 ROUNDS-00B-L07, #178 ROUNDS-03-L04, #179 ROUNDS-14-L06, #180 ROUNDS-14-L07, #181 ROUNDS-19-L05, #182 ROUNDS-34-L08. 5 rejected (folded): ROUNDS-00A-L09 into #1 (ROUNDS-00A-L01), ROUNDS-04-L05 into #168 (ROUNDS-33-L04), ROUNDS-14-L08 into #73 (ROUNDS-14-L02), ROUNDS-24-L05 into #103 (ROUNDS-21-L02), ROUNDS-26-L05 into #168 (ROUNDS-33-L04). A `<leaf-id>/<stage>` reference resolves on the leaf part. Verify the pin with `node scripts/conformance/run.mjs --catalog <path to capabilities.json>`.

## Decisions

- **T1. Transcribe the approved spec; spec text wins** (ratified). Terms, definitions, and labels are transcribed from spec 221-228, 415-425, 623-645, 752-811, 815-840, 966-1017, and 2491-2636, and only the gaps below are decided here. Where rounds-review src/data/glossary.ts differs, spec text wins: glossary.ts drops "according to stage" from the Pursuit label (spec 1004), and the registry keeps it.
- **G1. Name every version in the authority matrix** (ratified). The revision vocabulary (spec 754-764) adds the matrix versions: Opportunity Revision (786), Relation Version (793), Edition Version (794), Preference Version (802), Key Version (808), Activation Version (809), Capability Version (810), Projection Watermark (800, 811), and Algorithm Version (800, 801; also 811's "Projector version"). Entity Version aliases 781's "Provider/session version" and 782's "Profile/Entity Version"; Aggregate Revision aliases 789's "Expected-version command history" and 790's "Append-only accepted revision".
- **G2. Interview Round and Practice Item** (ratified). Interview Round is a Career Activity kind (spec 1497): "Interview Round" resolves to Career Activity, labeled with the kind option "Interview". Practice Item is pack-owned practice content keyed (pack, track, slug) per #39 (ROUNDS-07-L01), and #130 (ROUNDS-28-L01) owns the term. ai_coding_rounds rows are Practice Items.
- **G3. Claim and Attempt** (ratified). "Claim" aliases Extracted Claim (spec 834). "Attempt" labels only Practice Attempt (spec 1013). Execution Attempt (#3, ROUNDS-00A-L03) and Processing Attempt (spec 706, 803, 1168) are inspection-only.
- **G4. The Profile page is Account** (ratified). The current Profile page is Account (spec 405, 987). "Profile" alone is never a label; Career Profile is the only profile.
- **G5. Labels the spec gives two terms** (ratified). sharedLabels holds every option the spec gives two terms: "Role" (Opportunity 1003, Engagement 418) and "Opportunity" (Opportunity 1003, Pursuit 1004). "Role" stays as written, and SCR-ROLE asks the owner for distinct labels.
- **G6. Workspace means the Opportunity Workspace** (ratified-here). In UI copy, "workspace" means only the Opportunity Workspace (spec 989, 1433).
- **G7. Setting, Provider, Capability, and X or Y** (ratified-here). Account preferences are labeled "Setting"; "Preference" stays with the profile construct (Preference or Constraint). "Provider" is always qualified: Sign-in provider, AI provider, Calendar provider. In UI copy, "Capability" means only Share Capability. In "X or Y", the first name is canonical and the second is a label option.
- **G8. Labels for terms the spec leaves unlabeled** (ratified-here). A user-facing term the spec does not label takes its canonical term, a spec 966-974 destination, or its baseline label. Share Capability keeps the baseline "Share link".
- **G9. Software Engineering track names** (ratified-here). System Design, Coding, AI-Assisted Coding, Take-Home, and Behavioral live in a provisional pack.software-engineering namespace, with baseline spellings ("AI Assisted Coding", "Real World Problems", "Real-World Problem", real-world, builder, system) as aliases, until #39 takes the namespace over under pack ID software-engineering.
- **G10. Disposition vocabulary** (ratified). Features take Preserve, Transform, or owner-approved Retire (spec 335-337) plus an optional qualifier (spec 341-374). Data items take migrate, archive, rebuild, reconcile, or drop (spec 2666-2670). For #155 (ROUNDS-32-L01): bridge is migrate with a time-bounded adapter the transferring leaf owns, quarantine is archive, and retire is an owner-approved drop.
- **G11. Data-preserving clean cutover** (ratified). "Data-preserving clean cutover" follows spec 2637-2647: one bounded context at a time, one writable authority per converted concept, an explicit retirement criterion, and a time-bounded compatibility window. The two shipped migration comments that use the unqualified phrase for a drop with no data migration are allowlisted, not edited, because #1's lint (ROUNDS-00A-L01) bars editing shipped migrations. A new unqualified use fails. Revision 2 allowlists a third line, the verbatim quote of the catalog's ROUNDS-32 tradeoff in docs/program/non-goals.json, which #17's U11 register keeps word for word until spec-change request SCR-1 qualifies the catalog wording.
- **G12. Containment terms** (ratified). The five containment terms (Legacy Artifact Snapshot, Test Definition, Harness Revision, Artifact Renderer Contract, Share Capability) come from spec 623-645, 2491-2636, and 3212. If #2, #3, #4, or #11 merges first with a different shipped name, the registry adopts it and lists each difference as a spec-change item. At revision 1 none of them has merged and no containment collection exists (the only ROUNDS-00 work on next comes from #1 and #9), so the spec names stand and there is no spec-change item.
- **P1. Positioning** (ratified). The positioning statement is PRODUCT.md line 45, and its title form is "Career Command Center". This leaf rewrites README.md lines 1 and 3 and docs/architecture.md line 3 to it. frontend/index.html:17, Login.tsx:239, and SHOWCASE.md:3 keep adapter entries until #164 (ROUNDS-32-L10).
- **A1. Coverage set and adapter entries** (ratified). Every coverage-set name maps to a term label or an adapter entry: the 40 live and 3 historical collections, the user_progress.question_type and status values, the INTERVIEW_TYPES keys of interview_rounds.round_type, runner router prefixes and /health, literal App.tsx segments, Layout navigation labels and Command Center entries, literal eyebrow and title props at the 24 AppHeader call sites, and the six positioning lines. Retiring leaves: #110 for interview_rounds and its round types, #178 for the Profile and Settings pages, #43 for the nine content collections it adopts, the owning surface leaf for page, shell, and Command Center copy, and #164 by default. #25 decides users.target.
- **L1. Label module** (ratified). frontend/src/vocabulary/labels.ts exports a TermId union of user-facing terms, label(termId, { option, count }), inspectionTerms for inspection surfaces (spec 1016-1017), and specLabels with the spec 1000-1014 labels as written. There is no internal-term fallback: an unknown or internal term throws. New UI code imports it; existing copy keeps its adapter until its retiring leaf replaces it.

## Check Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `VOCAB_SHAPE_INVALID` | terms.json does not match terms.schema.json, or names an unknown category, namespace, or usage-rule term. |
| `VOCAB_TERM_ID_INVALID` | A term ID is not kebab-case. |
| `VOCAB_NO_OWNING_LEAF` | A term has no owningLeaf. |
| `VOCAB_TERM_UNDEFINED` | A term has neither definition nor definedBy. |
| `VOCAB_LABEL_INVALID` | A user-facing term lacks a valid label, a non-user-facing term has one, or an option key, default, or mapping owner is wrong. |
| `VOCAB_DUPLICATE_ID` | Two terms share an ID. |
| `VOCAB_DUPLICATE_LABEL` | Two terms share a label option that sharedLabels does not list. |
| `VOCAB_SHARED_LABEL_INVALID` | A sharedLabels entry names a term that lacks that label. |
| `VOCAB_ALIAS_AMBIGUOUS` | One alias resolves to two terms. |
| `VOCAB_ALIAS_SHADOWS_TERM` | An alias equals a canonical term. |
| `VOCAB_ALIAS_SHADOWS_LABEL` | An alias equals another term's label or label option. |
| `VOCAB_PACK_REDEFINES_PLATFORM` | A pack term, alias, or label equals a platform term, alias, label, or platform core name. |
| `VOCAB_RESERVED_LABEL` | A label breaks a usage rule (Attempt, Profile, workspace, Preference, Provider, Capability). |
| `VOCAB_SECRET_EXAMPLE` | A term example holds a bearer-shaped token, a /r/ share URL, or an email outside example.com. |
| `VOCAB_CATEGORY_EMPTY` | A scope category has no term. |
| `VOCAB_REQUIRED_TERM_MISSING` | A containment term, privacy class, core concept, or platform core term is missing. |
| `VOCAB_UNRESOLVED_REF` | A leaf reference is unknown or rejected in leaf-ids.json, a term reference is unknown, or a definedBy path is missing. |
| `VOCAB_LEAF_IDS_INVALID` | leaf-ids.json is malformed: counts, issue order, duplicates, or fold targets. |
| `VOCAB_LEAF_IDS_PIN` | The catalog given with --catalog differs from the pinned SHA-256 or leaf order. |
| `VOCAB_ADAPTER_INVALID` | adapters.json does not match adapters.schema.json. |
| `VOCAB_DUPLICATE_ADAPTER` | Two adapter entries cover the same name at the same place. |
| `VOCAB_ADAPTER_STALE` | An adapter entry matches nothing: its name or file is gone, so its retiring leaf removes it. |
| `VOCAB_UNCOVERED_NAME` | A coverage-set name maps to no term label or adapter entry. Add the adapter entry; never loosen the rule. |
| `VOCAB_NONLITERAL_COLLECTION` | A migration creates or drops a collection by a non-literal name with no adapter entry for that site. |
| `VOCAB_POSITIONING_STALE` | No line in a positioning file equals the terms.json positioning or the legacy line its adapter entry records. Lines are found by content, not number. |
| `VOCAB_CUTOVER_UNQUALIFIED` | A new use of the cutover phrase without "data-preserving" outside the allowlist. |
| `VOCAB_CUTOVER_ALLOWLIST_STALE` | An allowlisted line no longer holds the phrase. |
| `VOCAB_REVISION_MISMATCH` | terms.json and its decision record disagree on revision or compatibility. |
| `VOCAB_REVISION_NOT_BUMPED` | terms.json changed since main but keeps its revision. |
| `VOCAB_COMPATIBILITY_UNDECLARED` | A revision removes or changes a name, a label option (key, singular, or plural), a label axis or default, or a visibility, but is not marked breaking. |
| `VOCAB_REMOVED_TERM_UNADAPTED` | A breaking revision removes a name without a term adapter entry for it. |
| `VOCAB_BASE_UNAVAILABLE` | terms.json at the base ref (default origin/main) cannot be read. |
| `DR_RECORD_INCOMPLETE` | A decision record lacks a required field, a ratified record lacks an approver or approval reference, or a decision lacks alternatives. |
| `DR_RECORD_INVALID` | A decision record field has the wrong type or format, or its file name and id disagree. |
| `DR_DUPLICATE_ID` | Two decision records share an id. |
| `DR_NUMBER_RESERVED` | DR-0002 or DR-0003 is produced by a leaf other than ROUNDS-01-L02 or ROUNDS-01-L03. |
| `DR_APPROVAL_STALE` | A governed file no longer matches the SHA-256 its approval reference recorded. |
| `DR_SUPERSEDES_INVALID` | supersedes names no prior revision, or lacks a supersessionReason. |
| `DR_UNKNOWN_PACKAGE` | An affected package is not in contracts/authority/packages.json (once #16 adds it). |
| `CONFORMANCE_DRIFT` | A generated file differs from what its rule generates. Run node scripts/conformance/run.mjs --write. |
| `CONFORMANCE_RULE_INVALID` | A rule module lacks id, owningLeaf, or check, or its owningLeaf does not resolve. |
